context: Draw the architecture of a research diagram service. Exactly 10 components in four horizontal layers: Clients contains Web App and CLI; Access contains API Gateway and Auth Service; Processing contains Orchestrator, Model Worker and Render Worker; Storage contains Project DB, Job Queue and Object Store. Preserve all 12 named directed dependencies: Web App -> API Gateway (HTTPS), CLI -> API Gateway (HTTPS), API Gateway -> Auth Service (Validate token), API Gateway -> Orchestrator (Submit job), Orchestrator -> Model Worker (Generate), Model Worker -> Render Worker (Scene), Orchestrator -> Project DB (Save project), Orchestrator -> Job Queue (Enqueue), Job Queue -> Model Worker (Consume), Render Worker -> Object Store (Save image), Model Worker -> Object Store (Read assets), Orchestrator -> Render Worker (Preview). Show the queue-to-worker feedback dependency explicitly even though it points upward. No invented relay nodes or missing dependencies.

Draw a UML-style sequence diagram for asynchronous diagram generation, with exactly five participants in this left-to-right order: Researcher, Web App, API, Worker, Storage. One participant header and dashed vertical lifeline per actor. Show these 10 messages in exactly this chronological order from top to bottom: 1. Researcher -> Web App: Submit prompt; 2. Web App -> API: POST job; 3. API -> Storage: Save job; 4. Storage -> API: Job ID; 5. API -> Web App: Accepted; 6. API -> Worker: Dispatch; 7. Worker -> Storage: Save diagram; 8. Worker -> API: Complete; 9. Web App -> API: Get result; 10. API -> Web App: Diagram ready. Return messages 4, 5, 8 and 10 use dashed arrows. All message arrows are horizontal and labels readable. Do not turn the messages into ordinary flowchart boxes. Chronology must remain unchanged during refinement.

Draw an incident-response workflow with exactly 17 nodes, preserving the labels and these directed flows. Receive Alert -> Validate Input -> Valid?; Valid? --No--> Request Details -> Validate Input (input correction loop); Valid? --Yes--> Classify Severity -> Critical?; Critical? --Yes--> Page On-call -> Investigate; Critical? --No--> Queue Triage -> Investigate; Investigate -> Root Cause Found?; Root Cause Found? --No--> Collect Evidence -> Investigate (evidence loop); Root Cause Found? --Yes--> Apply Fix -> Health Check -> Healthy?; Healthy? --No--> Roll Back -> Investigate (recovery loop); Healthy? --Yes--> Document -> Close Incident. The four questions are decision diamonds. Receive Alert and Close Incident are terminal nodes. Keep all 20 arrows and all three feedback loops. Use an easy-to-follow top-to-bottom main flow with side branches and distinct return corridors. Do not simplify away a decision or invent steps.
